name: Seedless
tagline: A roguelite that seals its prediction of your next move before you make it: be unreadable where it traps you, readable where it rewards you, and open the receipts at the end.
summary: Seedless is a premium roguelite about being predicted. Before each move, the Demiurge (a per-player predictor with a population prior) commits a hashed prophecy that includes the drand round, and builds the next room around it. Rooms are either matching-pennies Adversary rooms, where surprise beats the trap, or Newcomb Oracle rooms, where the chest is full only if the Demiurge predicted you'd be cooperative. Tells are probabilistic, and each floor discloses its ratio. The house's own mixing comes from verifiable beacons, with CURBy Bell-test pulses sealing each floor, so the player's choices are the only free variable. After the run, every prophecy opens: 'It called 41 of your 60.'
core_loop: Enter a fork -> the Demiurge commits a hashed prediction (with the drand round) to an append-only log and builds the room around it -> the client unlocks input only once it holds the commit -> read the tells, guess the room type, and choose to be legible (Oracle room) or surprising (Adversary room) -> drand resolves what neither side controls -> survive or die. At floor end a CURBy pulse seals the floor, and at run end the receipts open every prophecy for verification and sharing.
why_now: Certified quantum randomness became a public service in 2025 (NIST/CU CURBy Bell-test beacon and Quantinuum-JPMorgan certified randomness, both in Nature), and drand makes verifiable per-move randomness free. Generative world models (Genie 3, Oasis, Matrix-Game 2.0) made 'lazy-rendered reality' an engineering object. The roguelite boom (Slay the Spire 2 peaked at 575K concurrent players) supplies the audience, and the brief flags verifiable quantum randomness as an unexploited consumer gap.
mvp: 90 days. Weeks 1-3: a text prototype with commit-reveal over drand, measuring predictor accuracy on 200 testers across choice types. Weeks 4-8: a three-floor vertical slice with Adversary and Oracle rooms, a receipts screen, CURBy floor seals and a public verification page, using pre-baked world-model vignettes (any stutter must be real generation time). Weeks 9-12: a Steam Next Fest demo. Kill metric: if a coin-flip bot, an always-predictable bot, or a mimic bot copying the population's median mix gets within 10% of top-decile humans, there's no skill gradient, so redesign the payoffs.
stack: Godot or a web build. A per-player context-tree/n-gram predictor plus a small population transformer, retrained each season. SHA-256 prophecy commits in an append-only Merkle log. drand quicknet with client-side BLS verification, and CURBy pulses verified through NIST's Twine chain. Optional world-model rendering (Matrix-Game 2.0-class) on cloud GPUs for real 'unrendered' vignettes.
business_model: A premium roguelite ($15-20 on Steam) with free seasonal Demiurge retrains. No paid randomness or loot boxes. Year two, a B2B sealed-RNG/sealed-prophecy SDK for verifiable runs in other roguelites and on speedrun leaderboards. An aggregated, consented human-predictability benchmark goes to research partners, and per-player models are never sold.
risks: No skill gradient: coin-flip, always-predictable or median-mimic bots may score near top humans
Calibration: choices with payoffs may be ~90% predictable rather than Aaronson's ~70%, which makes Adversary rooms brutal unless Newcomb payoffs are retuned each season
Feels unfair: 'the game decided before I moved' may read as cheating unless the receipts land emotionally
Public tells invite solver bots; handled with an open Solver League rather than anti-cheat
Per-player predictability models are behavioural profiling that ad-tech would want, so they're never sold and research data is aggregated only
Simulation-escape mysticism could feed derealization or AI-psychosis patterns, so the tone stays playful and claims no proofs
Overclaiming the physics: the Bell-settings festival is never billed as evidence about simulation or free will
moonshot: Prediction receipts as a civic right. Any system that acts on a prediction of your behaviour (recommenders, ad auctions, insurers, cars) must commit to its prediction before you act and open it afterwards. People get monthly receipts like 'We called 83% of your choices', and Seedless is where a generation first learned to feel modelled and manage its legibility.
best_line: A coin-flipper loses in Oracle rooms because an unpredictable agent gets empty boxes. The skill is selective legibility: be readable when cooperation pays and opaque when it doesn't.
